model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on standalone equity, subsidiaries added in the bridge

equity_bridge.item: Subsidiaries and associates: bank's share of profit not received as dividends, capitalised at 15x
equity_bridge.note: Consolidated profit after minority interest less standalone profit, with the stake-sale gains put on the same footing (they are larger in the standalone accounts): FY2026 Rs 832.99bn - 800.32bn + (45.93 - 30.27) = Rs 48.3bn; H1 FY26 Rs 423.39bn - 393.20bn + 15.66 = Rs 45.9bn; H1 FY27 Rs 494.74bn - 441.59bn + ~3.3 (72.88 - 68.79 pre-tax, ~80% after tax) = Rs 56.4bn; TTM = 48.3 - 45.9 + 56.4 = Rs 58.9bn retained inside SBI Life (55.31%), SBI Card (68.58%), SBI Funds Management (55.56%), SBI General (73.87%), SBI Capital Markets, SBI Payments, overseas banks, RRBs and Yes Bank (10.78%). Dividends paid up to the bank (mostly booked in H2) are already in standalone other income and valued in the flow. Same 15x and same method as ICICIBANK.NS; it is deliberately far below market: at 13-Nov-26 prices the SBI Life and SBI Card stakes alone are worth ~Rs 992bn and ~Rs 377bn, and the Q2 FY27 sale implies ~Rs 650bn for the SBI Funds Management stake, ~Rs 2.0trn or ~Rs 219 per share before any holding discount, against Rs 96 per share here. Investments in subsidiaries sit at cost in standalone equity, so nothing is counted twice.

equity_bridge.item: FY2027 SBI Funds Management stake-sale gain, after tax
equity_bridge.note: Rs 72.88bn pre-tax gain booked in Q2 FY27 standalone other income (SBIN.NS_Presentation_Q2-2027.txt:629), excluded from the core revenue base and margin; cash already received. After-tax amount estimated at ~Rs 60bn (tax on the gain is not disclosed). ~Rs 6.5 per share.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: below equity_5yr_cagr (16.5%, lifted by the Rs 250bn QIP, revaluation and AFS reserves) and far below the EPS CAGRs (recovery from the FY2018-FY2021 bad-loan trough); anchored on core net total income growth of 5.8% in FY2026 and 6.1% in H1 FY27 with NII running +14.8%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 16.5% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR 30.8% diverge by more than 30%: FY2021 EPS (22.87) was still depressed by provisions on the FY2016-FY2019 corporate NPA cycle, so the EPS and net-profit CAGRs measure a credit-cost recovery (credit cost ~1.1% in FY2021 to 0.37% in FY2026), not sustainable growth. Neither series is a usable forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on GROSS total income (CSV Revenue), FY2026 vs FY2023/FY2021. 'FCF' CAGRs use standalone net profit as the owner-flow proxy because bank operating cash flow is deposit noise; SBC is zero so reported and adjusted series are identical. FY2026 net profit includes the Rs 45.9bn Yes Bank gain.

scenario_narratives.base: Core net total income (NII + non-interest income, excluding stake-sale gains) grows 8% in FY2027: H1 FY27 was +6.1% with NII +14.8% and fees +14.9% but treasury income negative ex the SBI Funds Management gain; H2 laps a weak H2 FY26 NIM (Q4 FY26 domestic NIM 2.93% vs 3.11% in Q2 FY27). Growth then runs 11.5% as advances growing 17-18% earn through, fading to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR thereafter. Core pre-tax margin held at 41.7% of net total income (FY2025 41.7%, FY2026 41.7%, H1 FY27 41.3%): credit cost at a record-low 0.25% normalises upward while operating leverage offsets it. Each rupee of income growth is backed by Rs 2.10 of new equity (about 11.5% CET-1 against 13.3% today and SBI's 10-11% history), a marginal ROE near 15%; the existing capital surplus is not released.
scenario_narratives.bull: Advances keep growing in the mid-teens, deposits reprice down and the NIM recovers toward 3.2-3.3%: income growth 9.5% in FY2027, 13% for two years, fading to 7.5%. Pre-tax margin rises from 42.5% to 45% as the cost-to-income ratio falls below 47% and credit cost stays under 0.4%. New growth is capitalised at Rs 1.95 of equity per rupee of income (about 10.7% CET-1, where SBI ran through FY2020-FY2025), a marginal ROE near 17%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The credit cycle turns: credit cost returns from 0.25% toward 0.8-1.0% (it was above 2% in FY2018-FY2019, when SBI reported a loss and GNPA of 10.9%), the ECL transition adds provisions, CASA keeps sliding from 38% and the credit-deposit gap (advances +17.8% vs deposits +12.3%) forces costlier funding. Income growth 7-8% fading to 6%; pre-tax margin falls from 41% to 37%. The bank holds today's capital intensity on new growth, Rs 2.25 of equity per rupee of income (about 12.3% CET-1), a marginal ROE near 12%, at the cost of equity, so growth adds nothing.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SBI is valued as a standalone bank earning ~15-16% on stated equity, discounted at a 12.5% INR cost of equity, plus its subsidiaries at a deliberately conservative 15x undistributed profit. At that rate a mid-teens ROE growing with nominal GDP is worth roughly 1.4-1.5x book, close to where the market prices it; the valuation question is whether today's record-low credit cost and 41-42% pre-tax margin persist, not growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cost: at 0.25% it is a cyclical low; each 0.25 point on Rs 52trn of advances is ~Rs 130bn pre-tax, about 5 points of the pre-tax margin and roughly 12% of value

Subsidiary bridge is ~Rs 96 per share at 15x undistributed profit; a market-value sum-of-parts of the listed stakes (SBI Life, SBI Card, SBI Funds Management) with a 25% holding discount would add roughly Rs 100-130 per share
Cost of equity: the market price implies a rate nearer 11-12%; at 11% the base value rises by about a quarter
Capital intensity: every 0.1 of marginal equity per rupee of income moves value a few percent; the ECL transition and any change in risk weights shift it
Treasury income swings (Rs 30bn ex-gain in H1 FY27 vs Rs 92bn a year earlier) make single-year margins noisy
Core tax rate assumed 25%; pre-tax figure for H1 FY27 derived from disclosed tax and net profit

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 933.9-1234.7. Subsidiary quotes (SBILIFE.NS, SBICARD.NS) from the same API at the same session.
data_sources.financials: Standalone and consolidated accounts: SBIN.NS_Annual_FY2026.txt (P&L 11858-11886, provisions/tax 15428-15440, consolidated P&L 17940-17960, Yes Bank note 13477), SBIN.NS_Quarterly_Q2-2027.txt and SBIN.NS_Quarterly_Q4-2026.txt (press releases), SBIN.NS_Presentation_Q2-2027.txt (P&L 600-660, tax and provisions 780-800, subsidiaries 1413-1430, consolidated 1596-1627), SBIN.NS_Metrics.csv and the kpis table
data_sources.qualitative: SBIN.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-15), read after the drivers were set and found consistent; guidance items from its management-commentary section

inputs.share_count_basis: 9,230.6m equity shares of Rs 1 face at 30-Sep-26: 8,924.6m plus 306.0m allotted in the July 2025 QIP at Rs 817 (FY2026 annual report). SBI has no employee stock option plan at the bank level, so basic = diluted. Held flat: no buybacks, no further issuance assumed (CET-1 13.34% leaves no need for one).
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based compensation at the bank: SBI has no ESOP (the ESOP mentions in the FY2026 annual report relate to subsidiaries and to Yes Bank). SBC is zero, not unavailable; house and street values coincide.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY2026 standalone net profit Rs 800,320m (includes the Rs 45,932m pre-tax Yes Bank stake-sale gain) less the equity retention needed to fund FY26 core net-total-income growth of 5.8% at the FY2026 equity/revenue ratio of 2.25 (2.25 x Rs 133.2bn = Rs 299.8bn) = ~Rs 500.6bn. Actual cash distributed: Rs 141.9bn paid in FY26, Rs 160.2bn (Rs 17.35/share) declared for FY26. Interest income is the bank's revenue, not an excess-cash return, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime, 15:28 IST, final minutes of the NSE regular session; equals the 13-Nov daily close bar)

book_value.note: Equity = standalone capital + all reserves at 30-Sep-26 (includes ~Rs 344bn fixed-asset revaluation reserve and AFS reserve; the bank's own BVPS of Rs 512.31 at Mar-26 and its 18.6% ROE exclude those). On stated average equity FY2026 ROE is ~16.2% including the Yes Bank gain, ~15.5% core.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity of 12.5% in all three scenarios; risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights. Same rate as ICICIBANK.NS, KOTAKBANK.NS, IBN and HDB so the Indian banks compare directly; SBI's public-sector governance and cyclicality are carried in the heavier bear weight, not in the rate, and its sovereign backing and deposit franchise argue against a premium. Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.85-0.9 x India total equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% = ~12.3-12.6%. It is a cost of equity, not a WACC: the flow is after all funding costs. Terminal growth 6.5% nominal INR (5.5% bear).
inputs.lease_treatment: None separate. Indian GAAP: rent is an operating expense inside profit before tax; no lease liability.
inputs.nci_treatment: Standalone accounts: no minority interest in the flow. The bank's share of subsidiaries and associates is added once, in equity_bridge, as the part of their profit that does not already reach the standalone P&L as dividends (consolidated profit is after minority interest).
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift' (residual income on tangible book). Implemented as its algebraic equivalent, FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (ICICIBANK.NS, KOTAKBANK.NS, IBN, HDB, USB, WFC). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model. Deposits (Rs 62.8trn) and borrowings are operating funding: net_debt, total_debt and cash are 0 by convention, not by measurement. BASIS: STANDALONE bank (what SBIN.NS_Metrics.csv carries) plus a subsidiary bridge, the ICICIBANK.NS treatment. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = CORE net total income = NII Rs 1,731,205m + other income Rs 734,435m - Yes Bank exceptional gain Rs 45,932m = Rs 2,419,708m for FY2026 (SBIN.NS_Annual_FY2026.txt:11858-11868, 13477). The CSV 'Revenue' of Rs 5,562,410m is GROSS total income before interest expense and is not the base. FY2025 same basis Rs 2,286,481m (+5.8% in FY2026). H1 FY27 Rs 1,311,240m reported, Rs 1,238,360m excluding the Rs 72,880m SBI Funds Management stake-sale gain, vs Rs 1,167,278m in H1 FY26 ex Yes Bank = +6.1% (NII +14.8%, fees +14.9%, treasury line Rs 103bn incl. the gain, i.e. ~Rs 30bn ex-gain vs Rs 92bn ex-Yes a year earlier). 'ebitda' = core profit before tax: FY2026 net profit Rs 800,320m + tax Rs 254,448m (current 29,045cr less deferred 3,600cr) - exceptional Rs 45,932m = Rs 1,008,836m = 41.69% of core revenue; FY2025 Rs 952,712m = 41.67%; H1 FY27 (Rs 441,590m + tax Rs 143,320m - Rs 72,880m) = Rs 512,030m = 41.3%. da 0 (depreciation inside PBT; branch/IT capex funded within it). Tax 24.1% FY2026 and 24.5% H1 FY27 (both flattered by lower-taxed gains) -> 25.0% forward (statutory 25.17%). 'capex' = equity retained to fund growth = k x g/(1+g), with standalone equity Rs 5,444,420m / Rs 2,419,708m = 2.25 at 31-Mar-26 (CET-1 12.29%); 2.34 on Sep-26 equity over TTM core revenue (CET-1 13.34%). FY0 check: 41.69% x (1 - 0.25) x 2,419,708 = Rs 756.6bn core net profit = Rs 82.0 per share vs Rs 87.59 reported including the gain. ANCHORS (Q2 FY27 results, 30-Sep-26): advances Rs 52.1trn +17.8% YoY, deposits Rs 62.8trn +12.3%, CASA 38.32% (46% in FY2021), domestic NIM 3.11% (H1 3.06%), cost/income 48.3% H1, credit cost 0.22% Q2 / 0.25% H1, slippage 0.50%, GNPA 1.39%, NNPA 0.36%, PCR 74.4% (91.8% with AUCA), CET-1 13.34%, CRAR 16.09%. H1 FY27 standalone PAT Rs 441.6bn (+12.3%), consolidated Rs 494.7bn (+16.9%). GUIDANCE (SBIN.NS_Analysis.json, management commentary): FY2027 credit growth 13-15% maintained, ROA above 1.0-1.1%, slippage ratio below 0.6%; the filings themselves carry only a macro outlook. Loan growth of 13-15% with deposits at +12% and a flat-to-recovering NIM is what the base income path of 8% then 11.5% assumes. ONE-OFFS: Yes Bank 13.18% stake sale Sep-2025 (Rs 45.9bn standalone gain, FY2026) and SBI Funds Management stake sale from 61.86% to 55.56% in Q2 FY27 (Rs 72.9bn standalone gain) are excluded from the revenue base and margin; the FY27 gain is added once in the bridge. Capital surplus above the scenario's marginal CET-1 is not released. band_position: SBC is zero, the house/street band collapses. SBIN.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-15) was written while this model was being built and checked against it afterwards: unsecured retail/agri/SME seasoning risk, ECL and Basel transition, government ownership, West Asia macro risk and subsidiary value all match the scenario drivers and weights; nothing in it moved a driver.

The bank holds today's capital intensity on new growth, Rs 2.25 of equity per rupee of income (about 12.3% CET-1), a marginal ROE near 12%, at the cost of equity, so growth adds nothing.

base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 210 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income: marginal equity / net total income 2.10 vs 2.25 actual at 31-Mar-26 (about 11.5% CET-1 on new growth vs 12.29% at Mar-26 and 13.34% at Sep-26).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 against a house default of 15/50/35 and 20/50/30 for the Indian private banks. Bear is raised to 25% because every credit metric is at its best in the 12-year record (GNPA 1.39% vs 10.9% in FY2018, credit cost 0.22%), advances are growing 5.5 points faster than deposits, CASA has fallen eight points in five years, the RBI expected-credit-loss transition is ahead, and a government-controlled lender has less freedom over wages, branch footprint and directed lending. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs both a NIM recovery and a return to leaner capital while the bank is in fact building CET-1 (10.8% to 13.3% in six quarters).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
